network.tdh.spec.metadataDescription: The exact written form of the TDH rule, as proposed: every input, formula and rounding step, in readable form.
network.tdh.spec.title: The TDH v1.4 specification
network.tdh.spec.lede: TDH v1.4 is 6529.io’s name for its current TDH rules. This specification, P26, writes them out exactly, proposed as the rule every implementation computes to the last unit; section 11 lists every place it departs from 6529.io’s old backend, with the effect measured.
network.tdh.spec.mapDesc: Inputs (section 2) give the snapshot (4): the snapshot block is taken from the finalized chain, and the canonical events (3) are the logs in blocks up to it. Eligibility and rates (5) and identities (6) both feed holdings (7), which feed scores (8) and the day’s output (9). The parameter registry (10) feeds sections 2 to 8: contract addresses, sinks, the day length, editions and rates, the consolidation use case, group sizes and the four-wallet start time, and the boosts.
network.tdh.spec.s1.title: 1. Scope and conventions
network.tdh.spec.s1.body: TDH v1.4 defines, for one day, each wallet’s and identity’s balance, whole days, base, boost and final TDH per eligible token, and the network totals. Arithmetic is exact, with binary64 only at the ties of RATE and FINAL (sections 8.1 and 8.4), and every number and address comes from the registry (section 10). Ranks, xTDH, REP and upload files are out of scope.
network.tdh.spec.s2.title: 2. Inputs
network.tdh.spec.s2.body: One day’s inputs are Ethereum’s canonical chain up to the snapshot block, every event of four contracts up to that block, the edition-floor state of a fifth contract read at that block, and the rule version’s parameter list. Prices, Meme Lab, received xTDH, REP and $6529 balances are not inputs.
network.tdh.spec.s2.tableCaption: Four event sources and one state read
network.tdh.spec.s2.delegationEvents: Register and revoke, direct and through a sub-delegate
network.tdh.spec.s2.manifoldEvents: getClaimForToken, read at the snapshot block
network.tdh.spec.s2.topicsCaption: Topic hashes, keccak-256 of each signature
network.tdh.spec.s3.title: 3. Canonical events
network.tdh.spec.s3.body: Every event is read exactly once, decoded strictly, and put in one order that everyone can reproduce: block, then transaction, then log, then position in a batch. A node that cannot show it has every event must not publish, and a malformed event invalidates the day’s input rather than being skipped.
network.tdh.spec.s3.sinks: A mint comes from the zero address to any other address and debits nobody; a transfer from the zero address to itself moves nothing and is not a mint. A transfer to a sink, the zero address or 0x…dead in tdh-v1.4, is a burn. Sinks are credit-only: they receive records but are never debited and never consolidated. The FirstGM burn transaction is not credited to the zero address. Burns do not reduce edition sizes.
network.tdh.spec.s4.title: 4. Day, snapshot and whole days
network.tdh.spec.s4.body: Day N closes at N × 86,400 seconds, 00:00 UTC. Its snapshot block is the last block before that moment on the finalized chain, and ages are measured to that block’s time.
network.tdh.spec.s4.binds: The result binds (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash).
network.tdh.spec.s5.title: 5. Eligibility, editions, rates and seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.title: 5.1 Eligibility
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.body: Memes and Gradients count when their first mint, of any amount, is at least eligibility_min_age_s (86,400 s) before T; a transfer from the zero address to itself is not a mint. NextGen tokens count when minted at or before B. n_memes is the number of eligible Memes, a count.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.title: 5.2 Editions and floors
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.body: A Meme’s edition is the copies minted; burns do not reduce it. Below 300 copies minted it gets a floor, its claim’s totalMax up to 310, and counts at the larger of the two.
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.title: 5.3 Rates
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.body: Meme i: RATE(H, E[i]). Gradient: RATE(H, G), at least the registry’s gradient_rate_minimum (1.00), G = Gradients minted at or before B. NextGen token t: RATE(H, N_c), c = t div 10^10, N_c = tokens of collection c minted at or before B. With no eligible Meme, H = 0: Gradients get the 1.00 minimum and NextGen 0.
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.title: 5.4 Seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.body: Seasons come from the registry’s season_starts, the first Meme id of each season: 1, 48, 87, 119, 152, 181, 213, 246, 279, 311, 343, 375, 407, 439, 477, 516, 556. The list must start at 1 and strictly increase, or the registry is invalid. A season is listed for a day when its first id is at most n_memes; the highest listed is current. Seasons 1 to 20 carry a 0.05 bonus, and a season is boostable, that is, it pays, when it is not current and its bonus is positive. A new season must be added, as a new rule version, before its first card becomes eligible.
network.tdh.spec.s6.title: 6. Consolidation
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.title: 6.1 Events
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.body: Only delegation events with use case 999, for The Memes or the all-collections address 0x8888…8888, between two different wallets neither of which is a sink, count: a sink is never consolidated. Each event carries its block’s timestamp, the time of the registration. Every event’s position is checked, kept or not; two events at one position make the input invalid, and so does an event in a block up to the snapshot block stamped after the snapshot. Expiry, allTokens, token id and update events are ignored.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.title: 6.2 Pair state
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.body: Each unordered pair of wallets has at most one row. A registration in one direction is pending; the other direction confirms it. Each direction keeps the time of its wallet’s latest registration: registering again moves that time, and a revocation clears it. This is 6529.io’s own row plan (D136). The collection does not partition the state.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.machineDesc: Three states: no row, pending in one direction, and confirmed. REGISTER(a, b) creates a row pending from a to b; REGISTER(b, a) on that row confirms it. REVOKE on a confirmed row returns it to pending in the other direction, as the other wallet’s registration; REVOKE by the registering side of a pending row deletes it. Every registration also sets the time of its own direction.
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.title: 6.3 Identities
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.body: Confirmed links, newest block first and, within one block, by ascending pair key, grow groups in which every pair of wallets is confirmed; a wallet joins at most one group. Up to three wallets group as before. A fourth wallet joins only if the group of four then has one wallet whose links with each of the other three were registered in both directions from October 15, 2026, 00:00 UTC; a wallet that fails this is skipped, and no group holds more than four. P26 and 6529.io group wallets identically (D136).
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.checked: Checked against 6529.io’s own grouping code, run unchanged: the same rows and groups on 100,000 random link graphs and on every link in the delegation contract’s history to the October 18, 2026 cutoff. 6529.io’s stored rows, from its public API, group the same wallets. On that day no group of four existed: 499 groups of two wallets and 177 of three.
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.title: 6.4 and 6.5 Effective state and identity key
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.body: The grouping after all events up to B applies to the whole history of the day’s calculation. An identity’s key is its sorted lowercase addresses joined by “-”.
network.tdh.spec.s7.title: 7. Holdings
network.tdh.spec.s7.body: Three steps, in this order: an underflow test over the transfers before netting, transaction netting, and the replay of the netted transfers into each wallet’s acquisition stacks.
network.tdh.spec.s8.title: 8. Arithmetic and scores
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.title: 8.1 Rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.body: RATE equals half-up of 100n/d except at an exact half cent; with H = 3,941 that happens only for editions 8, 40, 56, 200, 280 and 1,400. The Gradient minimum comes from the registry.
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.title: 8.2 Base
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.body: Multiply the rate in cents by the whole days and round half up to a whole TDH. This equals the old backend’s two-step rounding.
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.title: 8.3 Boost
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.body: A record holds a token when the token is eligible and the balance is positive, whatever the copies’ ages. ADD’s first term and ratio come from the registry, and ADD stops growing once it reaches the limit of its rounded values; a program derives that point from the registry and must not hard-code it. For tdh-v1.4: ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 for n ≥ 33. The cent rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.title: 8.4 Final
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.body: FINAL is computed per token; a record’s final is the sum. Ties round down only for some boosts and some bases, the smallest being base 25 at 1.14.
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.title: 8.5 Totals
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.body: The total is the sum of identity finals, never of wallet finals. A second total leaves out the sink identities, one per registry sink, since a sink is never consolidated; sinks never enter any consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.title: 8.6 Daily rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.body: rate_e4 = beta × the sum of the rates of each copy with at least one whole day, in 10^-4 TDH a day; derived data.
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.title: 8.7 Range
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.body: A day is inside the tdh-v1.4 range when H, G, every N_c, every base × beta and the total are below 2^53, every net movement of section 7.1’s netting is below 2^64 (vector 50), and every balance and raw of a wallet or identity record, per token and in total, is below 2^64 (vector 58). Outside it there is no result. Inside it, hardware binary64 and exact emulation agree, and every output value fits 64 bits.
network.tdh.spec.s9.title: 9. The day’s output
network.tdh.spec.s9.body: The header (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash), and per identity its key, wallets, boost and final, with per-token balance, raw, base and final; the per-token final is what card-set credit uses. Wallet records, daily rates and totals are derived. The cycle root validators are to sign is restated below (P53, P28); conformance needs nothing more from those documents.
network.tdh.spec.s10.title: 10. Parameters
network.tdh.spec.s10.body: Every number the rule uses is a parameter of the rule version, read at its type; programs hard-code none. TDH v1.4’s rule version is tdh-v1.4 (D137); P26 called it tdh-v1.0 until October 18, 2026, when D136 raised the group size to four and added the two four-wallet fields. tdh-v1.4 is not frozen until launch: changes before it, such as D131’s netting and D136, stay tdh-v1.4, and from launch any change is a new rule version.
network.tdh.spec.s10.name: Name
network.tdh.spec.s10.hashNote: Recomputed with the Python reference; conformance vector 28 checks it. TH is P28’s tagged hash of the canonical encodings, defined below; P28 writes it H, and this page writes TH so that H stays the largest edition. The rows marked “formula” are not fields of the record: the rule version string tdh-v1.4 fixes them, so they are not hashed. The registry of tdh-v1.0, with three wallets, hashed to 0x74b4a8f9…63d3; that name is retired.
network.tdh.spec.s10.ruleIdNote: TH("6529.TdhRule.v1", keccak256("tdh-v1.4"), registry hash), P28 §4.5: the value a cycle root and a day’s feed file name the rule by.

network.tdh.spec.s11.title: 11. Where TDH v1.4 differs from the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s11.body: Nineteen differences from the old backend, each with the effect measured and the decision; DEV-11 is settled, since P26 now orders link ties as 6529.io does. On the replayed cycle none changes a value. DEV-2’s first case, tokens sent out and back within one transaction, changed two identities before D131’s netting; its second, a sale and a purchase in different transactions of one block, can still differ until the cutover.

network.tdh.spec.s12.title: 12. Issues found in the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s12.body: Fifteen issues found in the old backend, and what TDH v1.4 does about each: most are removed; BUG-7’s carry over history and BUG-9 are kept by decision, BUG-8 is fixed on 6529.io too, and BUG-15 concerns upload files, which TDH v1.4 does not define.

network.tdh.spec.s13.title: 13. Conformance
network.tdh.spec.s13.body: A program conforms when it reproduces all 104 conformance vectors (01 to 103 and 12b, as of 3bfa7b0) and, for a real day, the reference implementation’s output from the same inputs; a vector with no result asserts only that there is none. As of October 18, 2026 the Python and Rust references pass all 104, as do the Rust core and program B on the validator’s development branch (a1463f9). Each day’s page names the builds the daily comparison ran.
network.tdh.spec.decisions.title: Decisions referenced
network.tdh.spec.decisions.intro: The owner’s decisions these pages cite. The decision record is in 6529’s private design repository.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D112: The validator agrees on TDH once a day, peer to peer: each validator computes TDH v1.4 with the Rust core, signs the result and compares it with 6529.io. “Validator v1” is the design’s name; the software is numbered below 1.0 (D137).
network.tdh.spec.decision.D116: The validator code is licensed under Apache 2.0. It stays private until the owner publishes it, which is to happen before the first outside operator runs it; publishing it also publishes the ported TDH v1.4 core and its conformance vectors.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D118: Every validator checks each block’s events against Ethereum’s block headers, and the headers against a finalized block its own light client follows; a node that cannot complete the checks does not sign.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D119: Two separately written programs, A and B, are to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines; both are being built.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D121: One TDH formula everywhere: 6529.io, its backend and the validators compute identical TDH with the validators’ Rust core; the open deviations are settled as listed in section 11.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D125: Every validator is to compute TDH with two separately written implementations before it signs, and not sign if they disagree; anyone can add the Python reference as a third.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D128: A minimal Ethereum contract is to record a day’s result once both programs’ proofs verify. It is being built and tested against a fork of Ethereum mainnet; nothing is deployed until the owner approves.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D130: A new validator may take the TDH history from the network’s agreement, or check all of it itself.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D131: Ownership is read at transaction boundaries: within one transaction, each wallet’s movements of each token are netted. P26 §7.1 carries the exact rule.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D132: From October 16, 2026 the Rust core and the Python reference run daily beside 6529.io’s backend and are shown side by side; 6529.io switches to the Rust result about one week later, around October 23, 2026.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D136: TDH v1.4 counts consolidations of up to four wallets, exactly as 6529.io has since October 15, 2026, 00:00 UTC: up to three group as before, and a group grows past three only if one of its wallets has links with each of the other three registered in both directions from then. P26, the references, the Lean model and both validator programs follow, so the specification and 6529.io group the same wallets.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D137: Names: the rules the validators compute are TDH v1.4, 6529.io’s name for its current rules, with rule version tdh-v1.4; a new TDH version on 6529.io is a new rule version. The validator software is numbered below 1.0 (its code is at 0.1.0); “Validator v1” is a design name, not a release number.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.title: Evidence
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.title: Replay of 2026-10-11
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.body: From the live per-token inputs, TDH v1.4 reproduces all 132,481 wallet-token bases and every wallet and identity value. From the 388,335 indexed transfers it reproduced 10,278 of 10,280 identities and 11,128 of 11,130 wallets before D131; the two others were tokens sent out and back in one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting it reproduces all 10,280 identities and 11,130 wallets. The validator’s own Ethereum ingestion later read the raw logs from each contract’s deployment, with the history not yet fully checked: on them the Python reference with netting gives 2,061,888,816, the live total, and equals every live identity and wallet, and the second implementation agrees on every record. The input rules written out later, on October 15 and 16, change nothing on that input: its 414,007 logs pass every position and header-order check, every value is in its type, and the transfers of each log share their contract, sender and recipient. Nor does the four-wallet rule of October 18: the cycle’s snapshot is before October 15, so no registration is fresh and every group is as before.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.cleanRoom.body: The Rust reference, written from P26, its vectors, the reference README and the documents P26 cites, without opening the Python reference or the backend’s code, recorded 23 places where it had to choose (2 high, 11 medium, 10 low). P26 now states a rule for every one; the last, the state-read adapter for edition floors (F-10), was pinned in P53 §11.3 on October 16.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.comparison.bod: From independent inputs (Ethereum logs, history not yet fully checked), the Rust core is compared with 6529.io’s published files in every compared field. On the first two days, October 14 and 15, before D131: 10,280 of 10,282 identities and 11,131 of 11,133 wallets equal each day; the two others were tokens sent out and back within one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting: all 10,282 identities and 11,133 wallets, with totals equal to the uploads’ (2,070,436,337 and 2,073,214,934). Ranks, the balance and set-count columns (BUG-15) and display fields are not compared.
network.tdh.spec.symbols.title: Symbols
network.tdh.spec.symbol.M: The cycle’s boundary, N × 86,400 seconds: 00:00 UTC
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B: The snapshot block: on the finalized chain, the block b with ts(b) < M ≤ ts(b + 1) (section 4.2)
network.tdh.spec.symbol.T: The snapshot block’s timestamp; ages are measured to it
network.tdh.spec.symbol.days: Whole days, of the registry’s day_s, from an acquisition time a to T
network.tdh.spec.symbol.H: The largest effective edition among eligible Memes
network.tdh.spec.symbol.G: Gradients minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.Nc: NextGen collection c’s tokens minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.net: Address w’s net movement of one token in one transaction
network.tdh.spec.symbol.raw: A token’s whole days, summed over its copies
network.tdh.spec.symbol.base: Rate × raw, rounded: a token’s TDH before the boost
network.tdh.spec.symbol.sets: Full sets: the smallest balance of any eligible Meme, when every one is held
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B64: The nearest binary64 number; it decides ties
network.tdh.spec.symbol.SINKS: The registry’s sinks: the zero address and 0x…dead in tdh-v1.4
network.tdh.spec.s3.decoding: The event signatures and their topic hashes are in section 2.
network.tdh.spec.s7.property: The stacks depend only on each transaction’s net movement of each token per address (vectors 45 to 47). The Lean model proves it for transfers already in canonical order whose transactions correspond one to one; adding or removing a whole transaction is not covered.
network.tdh.spec.decision.legend: All settled by D121; DEV-2 amended by D131; DEV-11 settled by D136, which took 6529.io’s order of link ties. Adopted: TDH v1.4’s rule, which changed no value on the replayed cycle. Spec wins: on-chain order across transactions, netting within one. Old behavior kept: TDH v1.4 keeps the backend’s behavior. Kept, not in consensus: sink records stay, and never count toward consensus weight. Settled by D136: no longer a difference.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t1: No row, then REGISTER(a, b): pending, registered by a.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t2: Pending, then the other wallet registers back: confirmed.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t3: Confirmed, then either wallet revokes: pending again, as the other wallet’s registration.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t4: Pending, then the registering wallet revokes: no row.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t5: Confirmed, then the second registrant registers again: still confirmed, with that direction’s newer time and the event’s position.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t6: Pending or confirmed, then the first registrant registers again: only its time moves; the row keeps its position.
network.tdh.spec.s7.underflow: Exact rule, step 1: the underflow test, before netting
network.tdh.spec.s7.replay: Exact rule, step 3: the replay, after netting
network.tdh.spec.s3-1.title: 3.1 Log selection and positions
network.tdh.spec.s3-1.body: Every log of the four event contracts up to the snapshot block is an input, exactly once, ignored logs included. A log’s place is its block and log index; the checks below run on the inputs, before delegation events are filtered and before transfers are netted.
network.tdh.spec.s3-2.title: 3.2 Decoding
network.tdh.spec.s3-2.body: Three transfer events yield transfers, each decoded byte for byte from its canonical Solidity encoding. Every value has a type, and a value outside it, or written any other way, makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s3-3.title: 3.3 Order
network.tdh.spec.s3-3.body: Zero-amount and self transfers move nothing but are kept, because a zero-amount mint is how a card is created. Transfers in different transactions keep on-chain order, even within one block. Within one transaction, each token’s movements are first netted (section 7.1); section 5’s mint facts (each card’s first mint and minted count, G and N_c), the underflow test and the position checks read the transfers before netting.
network.tdh.spec.s3-4.title: 3.4 Mints, burns and sinks
network.tdh.spec.s7-1.title: 7.1 Acquisition stacks
network.tdh.spec.s7-2.title: 7.2 Per-token values
network.tdh.spec.s7-2.body: For each eligible token a wallet holds: its balance is the number of copies, its raw days the sum of each copy’s whole days, and its base the rate times the raw days, rounded. Tokens that are not eligible contribute nothing, not even balance.
network.tdh.spec.s7-3.title: 7.3 Records
network.tdh.spec.s7-3.body: A wallet has a record when it holds an eligible token or belongs to a group; an identity has a record when one of its wallets does. An identity’s balance, raw days and base are the sums of its wallets’, and its base is never recomputed from merged days. Boost and final are computed per record, so an identity’s final is not the sum of its wallets’ finals: two wallets that each hold one Gradient with base 100 have finals 102 and 102, and their identity, holding two Gradients, 208.
network.tdh.spec.s7.limit: The property stops at the stacks. Three things read the transfers before netting: section 5’s mint facts, the underflow test (vector 44) and section 3.1’s position checks. So a mint and its burn inside one transaction change no stack, but can make a token eligible and change editions, rates, balances and other holders’ TDH (the Lean model’s counterexamples H and I). Balances and raw days follow the stacks only while a token’s eligibility stays the same (section 7.2; not a theorem).
network.tdh.spec.evidence.difftest.title: Four-way differential tests, October 15 to 18, 2026
network.tdh.spec.evidence.difftest.body: Generated cycles ran through the Lean model, the Python reference, the Rust core and program B in six rounds. The findings of the first four were settled and pinned by new vectors: in P26, or, for an event’s default use case (E8), in the vector format and the references. In the fifth round, on October 16, all four agreed on all 30,000 main cases; its edge probes found one question for the vector format, which is still open (E13). The sixth, on October 18, ran TDH v1.4: all four agreed on all 30,000 main cases, 1,187 of them with a group of four, and found nothing new.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.fourWallets.bo: 6529.io’s own row plan and grouping code (planConsolidationEvent and extractConsolidations, at backend commit c2f4020), run unchanged, and the Python reference gave the same rows and groups on 100,000 random link graphs, with registrations before, at and after the activation second, repeated registrations, revocations, ties within a block and rows without times. On the delegation contract’s real history, replayed to the October 18, 2026 cutoff, both give 1,089 confirmed pairs, 499 groups of two and 177 of three, and no group of four. 6529.io’s own stored rows, read from its public API, group the same wallets: 1,277 of its 1,280 rows equal the replay, and the other three, confirmed in both, have another block and orientation in 6529.io’s table, from rows its earlier code wrote in 2023 and 2025; why is not established.

network.tdh.spec.implementers.title: For implementers
network.tdh.spec.implementers.body: No vector checks a root, and the rest of P28, such as the history root and the signature domains, is not needed to conform. The other vectors are to be published with the validator code (D116).
network.tdh.spec.changes.title: Changes since October 15
network.tdh.spec.changes.intro: P26 changed six times on October 15, 2026, once on October 16 and once on October 18. Two changes concern a real day’s values: the edition-floor correction and D131’s netting. The four-wallet rule of October 18 changes no day compared so far, since no group of four exists yet.
network.tdh.spec.changes.floors: Edition floors limited to Memes below 300 copies (section 5.2): a correction, caught before launch, of a text that as written would have raised Memes 206, 215 and 311 to a 310-copy floor and lowered 285 identities by 111,494 TDH on the October 11 cycle.
network.tdh.spec.changes.netting: Transaction netting (D131) entered section 7.1, then was made uniform; it brought the two DEV-2 identities of October 11 back to 6529.io’s values.
network.tdh.spec.changes.inputs: Four rounds wrote out the input rules that the Lean model, the four-way differential tests and their reviews asked about: log positions, logs given raw or decoded, and transfers at one log position sharing contract, sender and recipient (3.1); value types and how values are written in JSON (3.2, 10); cycle dates and the cutoff block in the header set (4.1, 4.2); ZERO to ZERO is not a mint (3.4); the claim limit’s type (5.2); a sink is never consolidated (6.1); the bound on balances (8.7); and a registry that programs read in full, with its constraints (10).
network.tdh.spec.changes.fourWallets: Four-wallet consolidation (D136) entered sections 6.1 to 6.3 and 10 on October 18: each direction’s registration time, links confirmed in one block taken by pair key, and a fourth wallet only through the fresh-link gate, exactly as 6529.io; the registry gained two fields, the group size reached without the gate and the gate’s activation time. The rules were named TDH v1.4, rule version tdh-v1.4 (D137), and the registry hash changed with them.
network.tdh.spec.changes.vectors: The conformance vectors grew from 35 to 104. The other changes leave every value of the October 11 cycle as it was.
network.tdh.spec.s9.root: Validators are to sign one hash, the cycle root (P53 §4.2): the day, its snapshot block, the rule version with its registry hash, the wallet tree, the per-token tree, and the counts and total. Two validators agree on a day when their cycle roots are equal.

network.tdh.spec.s9.leaves: Both trees pair adjacent entries left to right, promote an odd last entry unchanged and bind their leaf count into the root (P28 §3.3, §4.3, §4.4 and §4.12).
network.tdh.spec.s10.formulaTitle: Not a field of the registry record: fixed by the rule version tdh-v1.4, and not hashed
network.tdh.spec.s7.replayNote: Removal is from the end of the sending wallet’s list. After a move inside an identity an old timestamp can be last, and it is then removed first: this is the old backend’s behaviour, and P26 says it MUST be kept.

network.tdh.spec.versionRow.statusValue: A proposal, not yet adopted as a consensus rule. By the owner’s decisions 6529.io computes it from the cutover, about October 23, 2026, and every validator once validators run.

network.tdh.spec.decision.D120: Anyone can set up and run a validator with nothing run by 6529: the code is open source (D116) with reproducible builds, and the comparison with 6529.io is optional.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.day: N counts the days since January 1, 1970. A date names a day only when it is exactly eight digits of a real calendar date on or after that day.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.result: The day has no result until the block after the snapshot block is finalized too.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.ages: Ages are whole days of the registry’s day_s, 86,400 seconds.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.order: Header timestamps must strictly increase over every header a node reads for the day, adjacent or not; a decoded transfer stamped after T, in a block at or before B, makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s4.detail.example: Example: the upload dated 2026-10-11 is day 20,737, boundary 1,791,676,800.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.why310: The floor stands for copies still to come: below 300 copies, a final airdrop brings an edition to 310, above The Memes’ 300-copy minimum (the Nakamoto Threshold). An older claim of 300 gives 300.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.noFloor: From 300 copies on there is no floor, and a Meme with no claim has none.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.totalMax: totalMax is a 32-bit number, read at the snapshot block through an adapter that P53 §11.3 pins.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.detail.zero: A Meme with an effective edition of 0 is eligible but has no rate, and a copy of it in any stack makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.heroFacts: Not public yet: P26, its vectors and the Lean model are in 6529’s private design repository, and the vectors are to be published with the validator code (D116). Testable today: the registry hash (vector 28), and vectors 04, 06, 23 and 36, restated in full on the implementations page.

network.tdh.spec.s7.nettingRule.intro: A transaction is the set of transfers with one (block, txIndex). For each transaction and (contract, tokenId), `M` is its transfers with amount > 0 and from ≠ to, and every non-empty `M` is netted. (`M` is P26’s name for this set, not the cycle boundary of section 4.)
network.tdh.spec.s7.nettingRule.1: For every address `w` in `M`, a sink included: `net(w)` = the amount `w` receives in `M` − the amount it sends in `M`.
network.tdh.spec.s7.nettingRule.2: Sources are the `w` with `net(w)` < 0, each with amount −`net(w)`; destinations are the `w` with `net(w)` > 0, each with amount `net(w)`. Both lists are in ascending address order.
network.tdh.spec.s7.nettingRule.3: Pairing: repeatedly emit (head source, head destination, `k`), where `k` is the smaller of their remaining amounts; subtract `k` from both, and drop any head that reaches 0.
network.tdh.spec.s7.nettingRule.4: `M` is replaced by the emitted pairs, in order: each a transfer of `k` copies with the transaction’s block, timestamp and txHash, at the position of `M`’s first transfer.
